plaintext;">This is largely facilitated by two main operations:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">The first is tools/list, which discovers the tools available from a server. The returned catalog gives the agent information about the available capabilities, including their names, descriptions, and expected inputs.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">The second is tools/call, which requests execution of a particular tool with the supplied inputs.</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">For example, a server might expose a tool for looking up an issue in the issue tracker. A discovery service tells the agent that this capability exists and how to request it. Invocation asks the server to perform a specific lookup.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Such a shared interface makes integration simple. However, DoorDash still had to decide which agents can use which tools, whose account an action should use, and how access should be monitored. A coding agent might need access to GitHub, Jira, code search, documentation, and systems that show production behavior. Each connection introduces decisions about permissions, credentials, available operations, and monitoring.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">This makes the problem of tool access not just a matter of connection. Also, there are a bunch of company-specific rules that come into the picture here. MCP’s common interface doesn’t establish those company-specific rules. If every team implements these responsibilities independently, the same work gets repeated across many agents and servers. For example, one team might build an OAuth connection flow, another might develop its own secret handling, and another creates a different way to record tool usage. It becomes quite difficult to maintain consistent behavior.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">DoorDash organizes this problem into three separate concerns:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Access: </strong><span>Deals with the identity and permissions behind a request. The platform needs to know who is calling, what that caller is allowed to do, and which credentials the downstream system requires. For example, an agent acting on behalf of an individual employee may need a different credential arrangement from an automated process running for an entire team.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Tool-surface Curation: </strong><span>This concern handles the capabilities presented to the agent. A downstream server might offer hundreds of tools, while a particular workflow only needs a small subset. DoorDash needed a way to select the relevant, approved tools instead of exposing the entire catalog.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Operations: </strong><span>This concerns what happens when these integrations run in production. Teams need to understand traffic, failures, response times, usage, and costs. They also need controls that prevent excessive requests from overwhelming downstream systems.</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The Agent Gateway brings all of these concerns and responsibilities into a shared platform. Let’s look at that in more detail.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The Core Components of the Agent Gateway</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">A gateway is a service through which requests pass before reaching their destination.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">In DoorDash’s design, an agent sends its MCP requests to the Agent Gateway, which controls access and forwards approved requests to the appropriate downstream MCP server. Here, downstream simply means the system that receives a request after the gateway forwards it.</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: 100%;margin: 0 auto;"><table class="image-wrapper" width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" data-component-name="Image2ToDOMStatic" style="mso-padding-alt: column;align-items: center;padding: 0;width: auto;height: auto;border: none;text-decoration: none;display: block;margin: 0;"><img class="wide-image" auto;"></a></td><td style="text-align: center;"></td></tr></tbody></table></figure></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">There are two core components involved here: a proxy and a registry.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The proxy handles requests as they arrive. It verifies the caller, checks permissions, applies rate limits, attaches the required credentials, and forwards the request. It also produces information used for monitoring and auditing. Since it handles the actual request traffic, it is considered part of the data plane.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The registry stores the information needed to govern the incoming traffic. This includes details about the registered agents and MCP servers, ownership details, connection settings, authentication modes, policies, discovered tool catalogs, and configurations that determine which tools are exposed.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The registry is the source of truth for the control plane, which manages how the system should operate. The engineering teams use a management interface and API to configure the gateway, while the proxy applies the resulting configuration to requests.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">This division between the two components separates the work of configuring access from the work of handling traffic. A tool owner can register a capability and attach policy through the control plane. The proxy then enforces that policy when the AI agents need to use the capability.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">DoorDash also separates internal workflows and external-facing use cases into different proxy planes. They share libraries and registry concepts. But they maintain separate trust boundaries. Think of it as a common governance approach without implying that every request passes through one physical proxy instance</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Verifying Who is Calling and What They Can Do</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Two closely related concepts play a key role in the Agent Gateway built by the DoorDash engineering team. These concepts are authentication and authorization.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Authentication establishes the identity of the caller making the request. A request might come from a user, a software service, or an agent acting on behalf of a user. Authorization determines what that identified caller is allowed to do.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">These checks need more information than simply deciding whether someone can access an entire MCP server. A server may expose both harmless lookup operations and powerful administrative actions. The distinction between the two should be clear. For example, permission to search a repository should not automatically imply permission to use every operation the server provides.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">DoorDash’s agent gateway can evaluate permissions involving several pieces of context. It can consider the agent, the user, the requested tool, and the environment in which the request occurs. It can also distinguish access to read-only capabilities from access to capabilities that modify data. For example, a policy might allow an agent to read issue details on behalf of a user while preventing that agent from performing administrative operations. Another workflow might be allowed to run under a team identity, while a user-specific action requires the individual user’s authorization.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The agent gateway carries the identity of the caller through the rest of the request process, including routing and recording usage. That makes it possible to attribute a downstream action to the context that caused it.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Centralizing these decisions also gives DoorDash a shared place to change or revoke access if needed. Agent developers don’t have to encode security decisions in prompts. Also, each tool owner doesn’t have to rebuild the same gateway-level authorization logic.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Why Identifying the Caller is Different from Supplying Credentials</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Even after the agent gateway knows who is making a request and whether it is allowed, the downstream system may require its own credentials.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">A credential is something used to establish identity or access, such as an API key or an access token. The identity used to enter DoorDash’s gateway and the credential required by a third-party service are separate parts of the request.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">For instance, the gateway may recognize an employee through the internal identity system. However, a documentation provider may still require that employee’s authorization token before it allows access to their documents. There are four types of credential arrangements that are possible:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Internal Service Identity: </strong><span>This is an identity verified by the DoorDash infrastructure. It forwards verified caller context to internal services.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Gateway-held Token: </strong><span>This is a vendor or service token kept in gateway secret storage. It adds the token to the downstream request without giving it to the agent.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Per-user OAuth: </strong><span>This is for access that a particular user has granted to an external service. The gateway stores the grant securely, supplies the user’s token, and refreshes it when needed.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Service Principal: </strong><span>This is a non-personal identity used by software or team automation. The gateway obtains or issues short-lived credentials through a gateway-managed team identity.</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Credential injection means adding the appropriate credential to the outgoing request before forwarding it. The agent asks to use a tool. The gateway handles the credential needed to access the system behind that tool.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The design created by the DoorDash engineering team keeps raw downstream credentials, including vendor keys and OAuth refresh tokens, out of the agents. This gives the platform a central place to manage, rotate, audit, and revoke those credentials.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">How a User Connects an Account During a Tool Call</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Some tools need to act within a particular user’s account. For example, reading that user’s documents or updating a ticket as that user requires appropriate user authorization.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">OAuth is a mechanism through which a user authorizes an application to access a service with specified permissions. The application receives tokens that it can use for the authorized access.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The access token is used when making requests. A refresh token, when issued, allows the application to obtain a replacement access token when the current one expires.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Before the agent gateway, the product teams within DoorDash tended to build their own connection flows and token storage. However, the gateway centralizes this work.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">When a call needs authorization that is not yet available, the gateway starts the provider’s OAuth flow. After the user authorizes access, the gateway stores the resulting tokens in encrypted form and supplies the appropriate token on future calls.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">For clients that support MCP elicitation, the gateway can ask the client to present a connection prompt while keeping the original tool request open. The user completes authorization in a browser. The gateway then obtains and stores the token, resumes the original request with that token, and returns the result from the tool.</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: plaintext;">To clarify things here, elicitation is the protocol mechanism used to request the user interaction needed to continue the task. The user completes the provider’s authorization flow. However, the agent doesn’t receive the raw credential.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">For clients without elicitation support, the gateway returns a structured response explaining that authorization is required, along with a connection URL. This gives the client a clear way to recover, even though it cannot use the same pause-and-resume interaction.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Why Agents Should See a Selected Tool Catalog</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Permissions determine which actions are allowed, but the tool surface shown to an agent also affects its behavior.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Tool surface means the set of tools presented to an agent, including their names, descriptions, and organization. A server’s complete catalog may contain administrative functions, billing operations, destructive actions, and features unrelated to the agent’s task. Presenting all of those capabilities creates unnecessary choices. The model has more descriptions to interpret and more potentially similar tools to distinguish. The approach used by the DoorDash engineering team is to expose smaller, relevant catalogs that match the work being performed.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">There are two mechanisms behind this: bundles and filters.</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: 100%;margin: 0 auto;"><table class="image-wrapper" width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" data-component-name="Image2ToDOMStatic" auto;"></a></td><td style="text-align: center;"></td></tr></tbody></table></figure></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">A bundle combines tools from multiple MCP servers behind one logical MCP endpoint. An endpoint is the address to which the client sends requests. For example, a developer-tools bundle can provide selected GitHub, Jira, observability, code-search, and documentation capabilities through one gateway address. The tools still run through their respective downstream servers. However, the bundle gives the agent one organized interface through which to discover and use them.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Filters determine which tools appear in that interface. Their decisions can depend on the bundle, agent, user group, environment, or intended audience. A provider might expose both issue lookup and administrative operations, while a particular bundle includes only the approved issue-related capabilities.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The agent gateway can also give tools stable names and clearer descriptions. When names from different servers overlap, namespacing or aliases can help distinguish them. Namespacing means adding identifying context to a name, such as identifying the service to which a tool belongs.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">What Happens During Discovery and Execution</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Discovery and execution are related, but they happen at different points and require their own checks and validations.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">During discovery, the agent sends tools/list to a bundle endpoint. The gateway gathers tool information from the servers included in that bundle. This is known as fan-out, meaning that one incoming request leads to requests across multiple downstream servers.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The gateway then applies authorization and filtering rules. It combines the approved tools into a coherent catalog, adjusts names where necessary, and returns the result to the agent. The agent might therefore receive a catalog containing repository tools from one server, issue tools from another, and log-query tools from a third. It interacts with the gateway’s combined interface instead of managing each server’s setup separately.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">When the agent chooses a tool, it sends a tools/call request to the gateway. The gateway checks policy again, applies the relevant rate limits, determines the correct downstream server, and supplies the required credential. It then forwards the request and returns the result.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">A tool appearing in a discovery response doesn’t remove the need to authorize its execution.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">In other words, discovery controls what is presented to the agent. Invocation controls whether a particular request is allowed to proceed.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">This gives the gateway responsibility for both the available catalog and the actual use of its tools. It also means the agent doesn’t need to implement downstream routing. Neither does it have to select credentials for each provider.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Understanding What Happened After a Request</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Once many agents have used many tools, the teams need to understand more about the resulting activity. This comes under the area of observability, which means the ability to understand a running system through the information it produces.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The gateway acts as a useful component for this because all tool requests pass through it. It can record a structured event for each call, with consistent fields describing the server, tool, bundle, owner, and identities involved. For reference, a structured event is a record with defined fields that can be searched or aggregated. Along with identity and ownership, an event can also contain the authorization result, request status, error source, timing information, and request and response sizes.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">This helps answer questions such as which agent generated a request, which tool failed, and which team owns the affected capability.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The gateway also produces metrics, which summarize behavior across requests. This includes request counts, tool response times, authorization decisions, OAuth refresh outcomes, rate-limit decisions, and downstream failures.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">These different forms of information serve different groups within the enterprise. Security teams can audit access, platform teams can investigate unusually active agents, and tool owners can understand adoption and failures.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Making the Platform Easy for Teams to Adopt</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">A centralized gateway is useful only if teams can use it without excessive effort. Therefore, DoorDash makes registration and configuration for the gateway available through a self-service management interface and API.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Here’s how the process works:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">A team starts by registering its MCP server. The platform discovers the server’s raw catalog through tools/list, after which the tools intended for exposure are selected and approved.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">The team attaches the authentication mode, ownership information, and access policy.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">Approved tools are then added to one or more bundles. Once agents begin using them, teams can inspect traffic, response times, failures, authorization decisions, and cost information.</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">As we can see, registration is the beginning of onboarding. Discovering that a server offers a capability doesn’t automatically mean that every agent receives access to it. Ownership information is also part of making the system operationally useful. When a capability fails or needs a policy change, the platform needs a clear association between that capability and the team responsible for it.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">The gateway has now become the default path for agent-tool access across DoorDash engineering teams. DoorDash has reported more than 200 registered MCP servers, more than 30 agents and services used by thousands of employees, and millions of tool calls each week.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">What DoorDash Plans to Improve Next</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">DoorDash is making further investments in the gateway.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">One planned improvement is stronger agent identity and user delegation. Delegation means allowing an agent to perform an action on someone else’s behalf within defined permissions.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">DoorDash’s target model gives each agent a cryptographic identity and uses short-lived delegated credentials scoped to the user, agent, task, and target tool. This would make it possible to determine the connection between the user requesting work, the agent performing it, and the specific action being authorized.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Another planned improvement is dynamic tool discovery. Existing bundles already narrow the tools available to an agent. Dynamic discovery would narrow that selection further using the current task, access policy, and usage signals, so the agent receives the capabilities most likely to help with its present work.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">There are also plans to improve evaluation of tool quality and security, identifying risky descriptions, detecting secrets or personally identifiable information in errors, simplifying server creation and registration, and producing redacted tool-call event streams.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">These investments extend the same architectural approach. As agents gain access to more systems, the platform needs precise ways to establish who is acting, expose useful capabilities, authorize specific actions, and make the resulting activity understandable.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><strong>References</strong></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: item.title: Why has Shopify dropped React Native?
item.author: The Pragmatic Engineer <pragmaticengineer+deepdives@substack.com>

Feel free to share the link with colleagues who build mobile apps, or work on them.</em></p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>Recently, Shopify dropped the bombshell announcement that </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/c991f81f-220f-426d-9d11-9b8479ef5325?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Native is now the future of mobile development</a><span> at the e-commerce platform. This triggered a lot of reaction in the mobile development community, on the scale of the stir Shopify generated when it originally </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a70fddc7-2ef6-4b62-a617-97fb3773adad?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">moved over to React Native</a><span> six years ago.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>But times have changed, and we all know the agent of change this time: AI agents! This latest generation of models has improved in coding capability to the extent that Shopify no longer is satisfied with React Native (RN), as it was only </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/be222a8b-16fb-447f-a675-1442b3590f8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">last year</a><span>.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">This article looks into what led here, why Shopify made the change, and also the broader mobile ecosystem. We cover:</p><ol style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Why Shopify chose React Native in 2020. </strong><span>Android apps took too long to build, first and foremost, and it was nice to have consistent iOS and Android apps.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Still happy five years later. </strong><span>Shopify moved all six apps over to RN and most things were going well, and the 2020 move was seen as a good move.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Why ditch React Native now?</strong><span> AI is now very good at writing mobile code as well as backend code, while React Native adds abstractions that native does not. Shopify rewrote the Shop app to native in just 12 weeks(!!). Additional details from the Shopify mobile team.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Haven’t we seen this back-and-forth before? </strong><span>Airbnb did something similar by adopting React Native in 2016 before moving back to native just two years later. The underlying reason was the same: performance.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Going native since 2019.</strong><span> Moving to native used to take a long time, and Notion has been at it for seven years. When Notion finishes the process, a fair question will be whether a native editor actually slows down their web iteration speed, with or without AI.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) would like a word. </strong><span>KMP allows the writing of business logic in Kotlin and sharing it across iOS and Android while each platform stays native. It’s a technology that feels relevant, and could become more popular with AI.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>What’s next? </strong><span>It’s easier to write native iOS and Android apps than before, but that’s also true for React, Flutter, and KMP apps.</span></p></li></ol><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">1. Why Shopify chose React Native in 2020</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>Let’s rewind to 2020, when Shopify decided to go all-in on React Native (RN). Back then, mobile was a very important channel for the platform, with seven out of 10 customers using it on mobile devices. As Head of Engineering, Farhan Thawar </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a70fddc7-2ef6-4b62-a617-97fb3773adad?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">wrote</a><span> at the time:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“Each quarter, the majority of buyers purchase on mobile (with 71% of our buyers purchasing on mobile in Q3 of last year [in 2019]). Black Friday and Cyber Monday (together, BFCM) are the busiest time of year for our merchants, and buying activity during those days is a bellwether. During this year’s BFCM, Shopify merchants saw another 3% increase in purchases on mobile, an average of 69% of sales.”</p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">With mobile so important, it’s no surprise the company built native mobile applications for iOS and Android; after all, native mobile gives full control of a platform’s capabilities, integrations, and performance, so why bother with cross-platform technology?</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">It turns out one reason was the delay in launching native apps on Android, which Shopify struggled with, along with other companies.</p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">When Android takes a year+ to launch: the Clubhouse fail</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">During the pandemic at the start of the decade, the live conversations app Clubhouse was a massive hit after launching in March 2020. The app was iOS-only for the first 14 months as the team was unable to release an Android app. And at the end of the year, usage absolutely exploded:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><span>December 2020: 600,000 global installs (downloads) (</span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/1e9cea12-e464-493d-bb43-7daaf88dd049?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">source</a><span>)</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><span>January 2021: 3.5 million global installs (</span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/1907f276-14d8-4134-a662-c38c10830448?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">source</a><span>)</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><span>February 2022: 8 million global installs (</span><a 20px;font-weight: 400;letter-spacing: -.15px;margin-top: 8px;width: 70%;padding-left: 15%;padding-right: 15%;text-align: center;"><em><span>Clubhouse app: voice chat blew up with Covid-19. Source: </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/6132caf9-c96d-45fd-b495-74bc78ac0688?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="text-decoration: underline;">TechCrunch</a></em></figcaption></figure></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Despite all that popularity, Clubhouse was unavailable on Android at the time!</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><strong>It took 14 months to launch a beta version of Clubhouse on Android</strong><span>, and by the time it did in May 2021, the platform had passed its peak a few months earlier and usage numbers were by then trending down. It took until </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/ddd029f8-71d1-4bee-8bc7-43529ab6b8f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">July 2021</a><span> to roll out the Android Clubhouse app globally – 16 months after the iOS version – by which time it was too late to catch the growth wave, and that spelt doom for the promising business.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">How did this happen? There were a few main reasons:</p><ol style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><span>Android is more complex to build </span><em>well</em><span> for than iOS: more device types to support, and much older OS versions to support with different APIs.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">Getting good performance on low-end Android phones was hard.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">I also wonder if Clubhouse’s team was engineering for a scale that never materialized. Perhaps they tried to build the “perfect” app to launch globally, but missed the growth wave, meaning the app ended up “over-engineered” compared to a different version that could’ve been released sooner, in a more timely fashion that benefitted the business.</p></li></ol><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Building a native Android app from scratch – even with an existing iOS app as a blueprint – was a challenge during the 2010s and early 2020s. Clubhouse is an extreme case of a business which went wrong, partly due to a sluggish Android launch.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">But customer habits could have played a part: at the time, most US startups prioritized iOS apps and features first because in the US, the most valuable users were increasingly found on iOS. Prioritizing iOS made business sense for companies with mainly US customers, but not for ones with a global footprint, where regions like Asia featured mainly Android smartphone users.</p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">React Native helped Shopify add Android support faster</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>Shopify’s first positive experience with React Native was in 2018 with the Shop app (then called ‘Arrive’). The company </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a70fddc7-2ef6-4b62-a617-97fb3773adad?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">summarized</a><span> (emphasis mine):</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>“At the end of 2018, we decided to rewrite one of our most popular consumer apps, Arrive (which is now Shop app) in React Native. Arrive is no slouch; it’s a highly rated, </span><strong>high performing app that has millions of downloads on iOS. It was a good candidate because we didn’t have an Android version</strong><span>. Our efforts would help us reach all of the Android users who were clamoring for Arrive. It’s now React Native on both iOS and Android and shares 95% of the same code. We’ll do a deep dive into Arrive in a future blog post.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">So far, this rewrite resulted in:</p></blockquote><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">fewer crashes on iOS than our native iOS app</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">an Android version launched</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">a team composed of mobile + non-mobile developers.”</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Moving over to React Native was one of the easiest ways to speed up the rollout of Android versions of new apps. In 2020, when Shopify announced the move, that was the stated intention:</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>“Our popular Shopify Ping app (now called Shopify Inbox) which has enabled hundreds of thousands of customer conversations </span><strong>is currently only iOS. In 2020, we’ll be building the Android version using React Native</strong><span> out of our San Francisco office and we’re hiring.”</span></p></blockquote><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">2. The summary was quite the victory lap:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“To recap, we decided to switch to RN for three main reasons:</p><ul style="margin-left: 20px;margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Write it once</strong><span> - Stop building the same features twice, once on iOS and once on Android</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Talent portability</strong><span> - Enable devs to work fluently across iOS, Android, and Web</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Ship more value</strong><span> - Spend more time delivering value to users instead of chasing feature parity</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">We’re happy to share that our transition has been quite successful:</p><ul style="margin-left: plaintext;margin: 0;">Engineers are able to work across web and mobile allowing teams to do more with the same number of people and unlocked new growth opportunities</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;">Our apps are blazing fast (<500ms screen loads) and stable (>99.9% crash-free sessions)</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: native wherever it is the best tool for the job, giving us the best of both worlds</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: Mustafa explained:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>“Speed</strong><span>. RN apps are fast. We’ve achieved sub-500ms (P75) screen loads in the Shopify app. We’ve achieved similar performance in all our apps. Just like native, you have to apply good patterns and techniques to eliminate performance bottlenecks.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Hot reloading</strong><span>. This was one of our biggest pain points with native. Given the size of our code bases, it took several minutes for even the most trivial changes to be compiled and run on an emulator/physical device. This wastes time and breaks developer flow. React Native’s hot reloading completely eliminates this problem.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>TypeScript is awesome as the “shared” language for devs.</strong><span> TypeScript has become ubiquitous, and we’ve seen great success with developers transitioning between React web and React Native.”</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">There were also some new challenges:</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Worse debugging:</strong><span> “Debugging in React Native is flaky and configuring it correctly in VS Code takes some work. iOS and Android on the other hand have powerful debugging capabilities that just work”</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>Native code and devs still important</strong><span>. You want native code for performance-intensive code, certain animations, long-running background jobs and specialist APIs (like home screen widgets).</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;margin: 0;"><strong>More third-party libraries. </strong><span>“The React Native framework is not as comprehensive compared to Native, so you end up having to use more third-party libraries.”</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">But how quickly things can change in tech…</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">3. Why ditch React Native now?</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>There was widespread surprise this month when Shopify announced that </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/c991f81f-220f-426d-9d11-9b8479ef5325?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Native is now the future of mobile at Shopify</a><span>, meaning that RN is suddenly history.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">From Head of Mobile, Mustafa Ali (emphasis mine):</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>“In January 2025, I wrote that the future of React Native was bright and that Shopify planned to keep investing in it. That was true based on what we knew then. React Native was working well for us, and it remains an excellent framework. But since then, coding models have gotten dramatically better, and for our apps and our team, building </span><strong>the same feature in Swift and Kotlin no longer carries the cost it used to.</strong></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Native still means building and maintaining software on two platforms, that cost has not disappeared. What changed is that agents can now do enough of the implementation, translation, testing, and review work that it’s no longer the deciding factor it was in 2020.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>React Native apps can be fast. Ours are. We are making this change because agents have reduced the advantages of sharing implementation, while the advantages of building for each platform remain. </span><strong>Native keeps us closer to platform capabilities and first-party tooling</strong><span>, with fewer framework and dependency layers between our code and the platform.</span><strong>”</strong></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Of course, there have always been pros and cons in choosing native over cross-platform. updates done on the UI using expensive rendering operations. So, RN maintains a </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/5d28e97b-e454-49a5-8af0-dd275ee2b34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">React Host Tree</a><span> of visual elements on a screen (think a “logical tree”) which transform into a </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/47717174-d40a-40d9-9c87-ad048b07de6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Host View Tree</a><span>, the representation on iOS and Android. React itself cleverly minimizes re-rendering operations, which saves on compute resources.</span></p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Why performance necessarily wins with native apps</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">As mentioned above, a well-written native app naturally outperforms a React Native version. style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>React Native can </span><em>theoretically</em><span> be more performant, in the unlikely event the Native version has a poorly written structure, or if UIKit / Jetpack Compose or any other native library is inefficient enough for this to happen! But native has many fewer abstraction layers.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">One common question since Shopify moved to native is how come the Shop app had not moved over to the New Architecture to improve things like startup performance. I reached out to Head of Mobile, Mustafa Ali, about that. He told me:</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“We actually moved other big Shopify apps to the New Architecture. Shopify and Point of Sale were both migrated, and I believe we were one of the first large teams outside Meta to do it.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><strong>We got some performance gains with this migration, but they were modest</strong><span>. App startup got about 10% faster on Android and 3% on iOS, and some complex screens actually got slower until we tuned them.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>The team has </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/bf6795ae-2677-4d0c-bc91-e9cc06a9543c?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">written in detail about</a><span> the move to New Architecture. Nonetheless, being on native code provides a lot more opportunities to improve performance; after all, you can now control the </span><em>complete</em><span> rendering stack! Heck, you could also throw away the Apple-built system libraries like UIKit or ComposeKit and build more performant ones. Shopify doesn’t plan to go this far, but Head of Engineering, Farhan Thawar, told me they expect performance wins:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“I think we’re just at the beginning of how much better these native apps will be. I expect they will get faster – like with better startup time and more responsive interactivity – as we work through the codebase post migration.”</p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);overflow-wrap: anywhere;word-break: normal;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">One engineer, two platforms with AI</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">One benefit of React Native was that it wasn’t necessary to have both an iOS engineer and an Android engineer. But with AI, one engineer can build software on both platforms, Mustafa Ali told me:</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“One cultural benefit of switching to RN in the past is that we don’t have a separate iOS and Android team, unlike most native shops.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><strong>We have one team, and the same developer builds a feature on both iOS and Android.</strong><span> This keeps the context in one place and there’s no communication overhead.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">With LLMs making it easy to contribute code outside of your main expertise, I expect this to become more common in the coming months.”</p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Farhan put it even more simply:</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“Basically, React, as the shared language, is now replaced by the English language, thanks to LLMs.”</p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI more trivial with AI</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">Another downside of going native is having two codebases to maintain, which tend to diverge from each other in behavior, features, and bugs. But with AI, Shopify doesn’t see this as a big problem any more. Mustafa:</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;">“Maintaining two separate codebases was a big deal before LLMs, but not anymore.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>Agents are quite good at porting a feature from Android to iOS or the other way around.</span><strong> </strong><span>They are also good at comparing the two implementations over time. They can spot gaps in the code and in side-by-side testing, and fix them.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><strong>Shopify is also building a shared verification test suite to validate the two apps as identical. </strong><span>Again, from Mustafa:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>“We now have one shared test suite that validates business logic implemented in both Swift and Kotlin. This means that a feature can’t ship until it passes the </span><em>exact</em><span> same tests on both platforms. That logic runs headless on desktop, which gives agents a very fast feedback loop to iterate on.”</span></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;unicode-bidi: plaintext;"><span>Smart! It also confirms my sense that </span><em>verifying</em><span> code is becoming very important for working with agents, as is building dedicated verification layers.</span></p><h3
